types.embedding_query_text: Country: A nation with its own government, occupying a defined territory. Also called Nation, State, Republic. Examples: Iran, United States, Jordan, Bahrain.

chosen_type.label: Country
chosen_type.justification: Matches the definition of a sovereign state or nation.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: SingleFamilyResidence
candidates.comment: A type of house designed to be occupied by one family, typically detached from other homes. Also called detached house, single-family home, private residence. Examples: a suburban house with a yard, a standalone cottage, a bungalow.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

types.embedding_query_text: MilitaryOrganization: An organization responsible for the military defense of a country. Also called Armed Forces, Defense Force, Military Force. Examples: Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, Central Command, IRGC, CENTCOM.

chosen_type.label: GovernmentOrganization
chosen_type.justification: Best match for an organization responsible for military defense.

candidates.label: GovernmentOrganization
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOrganization is an organization or agency that is part of a governmental body. Also called public sector entity, state agency, governmental body. Examples: Department of Defense, Environmental Protection Agency, National Institutes of Health, local city council.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: EducationalOrganization
candidates.comment: An EducationalOrganization is a CivicStructure that provides education. Also called learning institution, academic body, school. Examples: A university, a high school, a vocational college, a research institute.

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

candidates.label: MedicalOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization, physical or virtual, operating in the medical domain, such as a hospital or clinic. Also called healthcare organization, medical institution, health system. Examples: "Mayo Clinic", "World Health Organization", "Doctors Without Borders". Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group.

types.embedding_query_text: Person: A human being, especially an adult. Also called Individual, Human, Man. Examples: Jennifer Kavanagh, Andreas Krieg, Mona Yacoubian, Pete Hegseth.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: Direct match for a human being.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: IndividualPhysician
candidates.comment: An IndividualPhysician is a medical business representing a single medical practitioner. Also called doctor, medical doctor, general practitioner, specialist. Examples: Dr. Jane Smith (a family doctor), Dr. John Doe (a cardiologist), a local pediatrician. Distinct from Physician, which is the general role, and MedicalOrganization, which is a facility.

candidates.label: PeopleAudience
candidates.comment: A PeopleAudience, as an Audience, describes a set of characteristics belonging to people, e.g., who compose an item's target audience. Also called demographic group, target audience, human audience. Examples: 'adults aged 18-35', 'students', 'retirees'. Distinct from Audience, which is a broader category including non-human audiences.

candidates.label: Thing
candidates.comment: The most generic and fundamental type in schema.org, representing any item or entity. Also called entity, item, object. Examples: a person, a book, a place, an event.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

types.embedding_query_text: Date: A point in time, typically represented by a day, month, and year. Also called Day, Time, Period. Examples: March 1, July 8.

chosen_type.label: Date
chosen_type.justification: Exact match for a point in time.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

types.embedding_query_text: DayOfWeek: A day of the week, such as Monday or Friday. Also called Weekday, Day. Examples: Friday.

chosen_type.label: DayOfWeek
chosen_type.definition: A unit of time representing a day of the week.
chosen_type.justification: Perfect match for a day of the week.

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: PlaceOfWorship
candidates.comment: A PlaceOfWorship is a civic structure or building used for religious services and spiritual activities. Also called religious building, house of worship, sanctuary. Examples: a church, a synagogue, a mosque, a temple. Distinct from Museum, which is for exhibiting artifacts.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

chosen_type.label: MilitaryConflict
chosen_type.justification: No direct match in schema.org, but a common concept.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: NLNonprofitType
candidates.comment: NLNonprofitType is an enumeration for specific non-profit organization types originating from the Netherlands. Also called Dutch non-profit type, Netherlands charity classification. Examples: ANBI (Algemeen Nut Beogende Instelling), SBBI (Sociaal Belang Behartigende Instelling). Distinct from NonprofitType, which is a general enumeration for non-profit types.

candidates.label: UserPlusOnes
candidates.comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of giving a "+1" endorsement, typically on Google+ or similar platforms. Also called user endorsement, +1, social recommendation. Examples: a user giving a +1 to a web page, endorsing a business, recommending content.

candidates.label: DrugStrength
candidates.comment: A DrugStrength is a MedicalIntangible representing a specific potency in which a medical drug is available in a particular country. Also called medication dosage, pharmaceutical concentration. Examples: "500 mg tablets", "10 mg/mL solution", "25 mcg patch".

types.embedding_query_text: Organization Examples: Defense Priorities think tank, Center for Strategic and International Studies, Middle East Institute, CSIS.

chosen_type.label: Organization
chosen_type.justification: Best match for a think tank or research institution.

mentions: Center for Strategic and International Studies

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: FundingScheme
candidates.comment: A FundingScheme is an Organization that defines guidelines, principles, and mechanisms for grant-based funding to support projects and activities. Also called grant program, funding initiative, research funding framework. Examples: EU Horizon 2020, NIH-R01 Grant Program, Wellcome institutional strategic support fund.

types.embedding_query_text: University Examples: University of Bath, King's College London.

chosen_type.label: CollegeOrUniversity
chosen_type.justification: Direct match for a higher education institution.

candidates.label: CollegeOrUniversity
candidates.comment: A third-level educational institution providing higher education. Also called university, college, higher education institution. Examples: Harvard University, Oxford College, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Sorbonne University. Distinct from EducationalOrganization, which is a broader category for any educational body.

candidates.label: CourseInstance
candidates.comment: A CourseInstance is a specific offering of an educational course, distinguished by its particular time, location, medium, or target student group. Also called course section, class session, course offering, specific class. Examples: "Fall 2023 Introduction to Python (Online)," "Spring 2024 Art History 101 (Campus A, Section B)," "Summer Intensive Yoga Teacher Training." Distinct from Course, which is the general description of the educational content.

candidates.label: MedicalObservationalStudyDesign
candidates.comment: An enumeration of design models for observational medical studies. Also called observational study type, research design, epidemiological design. Examples: "CohortStudy", "CaseControlStudy", "CrossSectionalStudy".

candidates.label: UKNonprofitType
candidates.comment: An enumeration of specific non-profit organization types recognized within the United Kingdom. Also called UK charity type, British non-profit category, UK voluntary sector classification. Examples: a registered charity, a community interest company (CIC), a benevolent society.

candidates.label: PublicToilet
candidates.comment: A PublicToilet is a CivicStructure containing one or more toilets available for use by the general public, customers, or employees. Also called public restroom, public convenience, washroom. Examples: a toilet in a park, a restroom in a shopping mall, a public toilet facility at a train station, a highway rest stop bathroom.

types.embedding_query_text: AcademicDepartment Examples: School of Security Studies.

chosen_type.label: EducationalOrganization
chosen_type.justification: Best match for an academic department.

candidates.label: SchoolDistrict
candidates.comment: An administrative area responsible for the organization and operation of public schools within its geographical boundaries. Also called education district, school system, local education authority. Examples: 'Los Angeles Unified School District', 'New York City Department of Education', 'Springfield School District 186'.

candidates.label: School
candidates.comment: An educational organization providing instruction to students, typically for primary or secondary education. Also called educational institution, academy, learning center, college. Examples: a public elementary school, a private high school, a vocational school, a university.

candidates.label: FundingScheme
candidates.comment: A FundingScheme is an Organization that defines guidelines, principles, and mechanisms for grant-based funding to support projects and activities. Also called grant program, funding initiative, research funding framework. Examples: EU Horizon 2020, NIH-R01 Grant Program, Wellcome institutional strategic support fund.

candidates.label: EducationalOrganization
candidates.comment: An EducationalOrganization is a CivicStructure that provides education. Also called learning institution, academic body, school. Examples: A university, a high school, a vocational college, a research institute.

candidates.label: EducationalOccupationalProgram
candidates.comment: An EducationalOccupationalProgram is an Intangible program offered by an institution that defines the learning path to achieve an outcome, such as a credential or new occupational opportunity. Also called academic program, training course, career pathway. Examples: A Master's degree program in engineering, a vocational training program for electricians, a coding bootcamp, a nursing school curriculum.

chosen_type.label: GovernmentOrganization
chosen_type.justification: Best match for a government agency.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: GovernmentOrganization
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOrganization is an organization or agency that is part of a governmental body. Also called public sector entity, state agency, governmental body. Examples: Department of Defense, Environmental Protection Agency, National Institutes of Health, local city council.

candidates.label: GovernmentPermit
candidates.comment: A GovernmentPermit is a formal authorization issued by a government agency. Also called public license, state approval, official authorization. Examples: building permit, driver's license, business operating license, fishing permit.

candidates.label: GovernmentOffice
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOffice is a local business representing a specific governmental agency or department. Also called public agency office, state department branch, municipal service center. Examples: IRS office, DMV office, local planning department, social security office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is the physical structure that may contain multiple offices.

candidates.label: GovernmentService
candidates.comment: A GovernmentService is an intangible service provided by a government organization to the public. Also called public service, state-provided service, municipal offering. Examples: food stamps program, veterans benefits, public education, waste collection.

chosen_type.label: Place
chosen_type.justification: Best match for a geographic location, although not a perfect fit.

candidates.label: GeoCoordinates
candidates.comment: GeoCoordinates is a StructuredValue representing the geographic coordinates of a place or event, typically latitude and longitude. Also called geographic location, GPS coordinates, spatial coordinates. Examples: Latitude 34.0522, Longitude -118.2437 (for Los Angeles), a specific point on a map, the coordinates of an event venue.

candidates.label: OceanBodyOfWater
candidates.comment: An OceanBodyOfWater, as a BodyOfWater, is a large expanse of saltwater, such as the Pacific Ocean. Also called ocean, sea, marine body. Examples: Atlantic Ocean, Indian Ocean, Southern Ocean. Distinct from LakeBodyOfWater, which is an inland freshwater body.

candidates.label: VirtualLocation
candidates.comment: An online or non-physical location where events can be attended, such as a webinar or online meeting. Also called online venue, remote location, digital space. Examples: a Zoom meeting room, a webinar platform, a virtual conference hall.

candidates.label: SeaBodyOfWater
candidates.comment: A large expanse of saltwater, typically part of an ocean or a large inland body of saltwater. Also called sea, ocean, marine body, saltwater expanse. Examples: the Mediterranean Sea, the Caribbean Sea, the Black Sea, the Caspian Sea. Distinct from RiverBodyOfWater, which is a flowing freshwater course.

candidates.label: BoatTerminal
candidates.comment: A CivicStructure serving as a station for boats, ships, and other water vessels to dock and embark/disembark passengers or cargo. Also called ferry terminal, cruise port, marina, dock. Examples: "The Seattle Ferry Terminal", "PortMiami cruise terminal", "A local marina office".

types.embedding_query_text: MilitaryBase Examples: Prince Hassan base, King Faisal base.

chosen_type.label: DefenceEstablishment
chosen_type.justification: Direct match for a military base.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: Airport
candidates.comment: An Airport is a CivicStructure that serves as a facility for aircraft to take off and land, and for passenger and cargo services. Also called airfield, aerodrome, air terminal. Examples: London Heathrow Airport, John F. Kennedy International Airport, Tokyo Narita Airport. Distinct from Airline, which is the company operating flights.

candidates.label: Mosque
candidates.comment: A civic structure that is a place of worship for Muslims. Also called masjid, Islamic house of worship, Islamic center. Examples: "Blue Mosque", "Faisal Mosque", a local community mosque. Distinct from PlaceOfWorship, which is a broader category.

candidates.label: BoatTerminal
candidates.comment: A CivicStructure serving as a station for boats, ships, and other water vessels to dock and embark/disembark passengers or cargo. Also called ferry terminal, cruise port, marina, dock. Examples: "The Seattle Ferry Terminal", "PortMiami cruise terminal", "A local marina office".

candidates.label: TrainStation
candidates.comment: A civic structure serving as a designated stop for trains, where passengers can board or alight. Also called railway station, rail depot, terminal station. Examples: Grand Central Terminal, London King's Cross, a local commuter rail station.

chosen_type.label: NewsMediaOrganization
chosen_type.justification: Best match for a news organization.

candidates.label: NewsMediaOrganization
candidates.comment: A NewsMediaOrganization is an organization that produces and disseminates news, such as a newspaper or TV station. Also called news agency, media outlet, journalistic organization. Examples: The New York Times, BBC News, CNN. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any type of organization.

candidates.label: ArchiveOrganization
candidates.comment: An ArchiveOrganization is a LocalBusiness that maintains, preserves, and typically provides public access to archival materials. Also called archives, historical society, records center, repository. Examples: National Archives, a university special collections library, a corporate archive, a local historical society.

candidates.label: BackgroundNewsArticle
candidates.comment: A NewsArticle that provides historical context, definitions, or detailed explanations on a specific topic. Also called explainer article, backgrounder, FAQ document. Examples: "An explainer on climate change", "A detailed history of the European Union", "FAQ about blockchain technology". Distinct from NewsArticle, which reports on current events.

candidates.label: NewsArticle
candidates.comment: A NewsArticle, as an Article, is a creative work whose content reports news or provides background context for understanding news. Also called news report, news story, journalistic article. Examples: a breaking news report, an investigative journalism piece, an opinion column in a newspaper. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is typically less formal and often personal.

candidates.label: AnalysisNewsArticle
candidates.comment: An AnalysisNewsArticle is a NewsArticle that combines factual reporting with the author's expertise, offering interpretations and conclusions. Also called news analysis, interpretive news, expert commentary. Examples: An article analyzing the economic impact of a new policy, a piece interpreting election results, a report on scientific findings with expert commentary. Distinct from NewsArticle, which primarily focuses on factual reporting without extensive interpretation.
